description: Turkish Cay Black Tea is more than just a beverage; it is a symbol of hospitality and daily life in Turkey. Brewed in a unique double teapot, this strong and aromatic black tea is enjoyed throughout the day, often served in small tulip-shaped glasses. Its rich flavor and comforting warmth make it a perfect companion for conversations and moments of relaxation.

instructions.title: Prepare the Çaydanlık
instructions.text: Fill the bottom, larger pot of your double teapot (çaydanlık) with approximately 1 liter of fresh cold water.

instructions.title: Add Tea Leaves
instructions.text: Place the Turkish black tea leaves into the top, smaller teapot. Use about 3-4 tablespoons for a strong brew, adjusting to your preference. Do not add water to the top pot yet.

instructions.title: Start Boiling Water
instructions.text: Place the çaydanlık on the stove. Bring the water in the bottom pot to a rolling boil.

instructions.title: Brew the Tea Concentrate
instructions.text: Once the water in the bottom pot is boiling, carefully pour about 250-300 ml of this hot water over the tea leaves in the top teapot. Place the top teapot back onto the bottom pot.

instructions.title: Steep the Tea
instructions.text: Reduce the heat to low. Allow the tea to steep for at least 15-20 minutes. The steam from the bottom pot will gently brew the tea in the top pot, extracting its full flavor without burning the leaves.

instructions.title: Serve Your Cay
instructions.text: To serve, pour the strong tea concentrate from the top pot into a small, tulip-shaped tea glass (ince belli bardak). Adjust the strength by adding hot water from the bottom pot to your liking. Add sugar if desired.

instructions.title: Enjoy and Refill
instructions.text: Serve immediately and enjoy your authentic Turkish Cay. You can keep the remaining tea warm on very low heat on the stove, refilling glasses as needed.

tips: For the most authentic flavor, always use high-quality Turkish black tea leaves, such as Çaykur Rize tea, which are specifically processed for this brewing method.
Never boil the tea leaves directly; the gentle steam brewing method in a çaydanlık is essential for a smooth, non-bitter taste, allowing the leaves to fully unfurl.
Turkish tea is traditionally served in clear, tulip-shaped glasses (ince belli bardak) to appreciate its beautiful color and to keep it warm longer. Always offer sugar on the side.
